summary: Swarm smwgpu16s ENDED SOLVED with two accepted solutions (m2 on MC120's hinges, m1 on MC120 plus the equilateral collapse). My three v1 corrections stay retracted and were delivered to both members in their verdict reasons. Consolidated outcome of the block: (1) MC120 is accepted with STRICT aperture < 120 degrees plus the missing hypothesis W nonempty (a degenerate K_i empties W, and an empty residual forces W empty, so |J| <= 1 is |J| = 1); (2) the a.e. step is best formulated as m1's ENGINE, which consumes no rigidity lemma - W open, c = a a.e. on W, and positive average circle-section length in W already contradict Def 1.2, with the rotation-averaged Fubini step that m2 isolated being what licenses it; (3) the endpoint 120 degrees is genuinely open, my attempted extension was circular and is refuted by the Reuleaux configuration (W inside a Reuleaux interior has no unit pair while an open 60-degree outer window exists, and the two thresholds arccos(r/2) - 30 and arcsin(1/(2r)) are identically equal), with t0 = 1.9319 the exact coincidence point; (4) the decisive new result is m1's VACUITY of the equilateral case: three 3-label paired blocks with pairwise intersections at most 1 always cover all six labels, so J is empty and W must be empty, which I re-derived by inclusion-exclusion rather than by enumeration; the correct non-vacuous statement is that at most TWO such directions can occur. Remaining obligations, all source-level: (H)/O1 derive the outer-strip hypothesis and approach-radius compatibility from the Straddle geometry; O2 the boundary-slope condition at exactly 120 degrees; O3 the essential label convention. No global chromatic conclusion, no 6-colouring, no chi(R^2) bound.

verified_results: GRADE [P] RETRACTION R1: uniform outer-strip width on a compact subarc does follow. If the strip at base direction e of width delta lies in the open set S, then for dist(e',e) < delta/2 the strip at e' of width delta/2 is contained in the strip at e (the angular and radial ranges nest), hence in S; so the set of (e', delta) admitting a strip is open in the base direction and the supremum width is positive and lower semicontinuous, giving a positive minimum on a compact subarc. The parent has compiled this as outerAngularStrips_compact_radius in ConeGeometry with standard axioms, together with OA120/CC60 and a concrete consumer.

GRADE [P] RETRACTION R2, with the counterexample verified: A = (sqrt3/2,-1/2), B = (sqrt3/2,1/2), C = (sqrt3,0) are unit vectors at angles -30, +30, 0 degrees and pairwise unit apart. W = (open unit balls about A, B, C) intersected with {|z| > 1} is contained in the interior of the Reuleaux triangle of width 1, whose interior has all pairwise distances below 1, so W contains no unit pair; yet every theta in the open arc (-30,30) degrees has e(theta) strictly inside all three balls, and by openness a radial range (1, 1+delta(theta)) also lies in W, so a genuine outer strip of full width 60 degrees exists there. Hence an open 60-degree outer arc can be monochromatic with no unit pair, and my endpoint extension is dead.

GRADE [P] The sharp reason for R2, verified by identity: at radius r the maximal half-angle of a point still inside the disk about A is arccos(r/2) - 30 degrees (attained on the Reuleaux arc), and the half-angle needed for a unit pair at radius r is arcsin(1/(2r)); these coincide because sin(arccos(r/2) - 30 deg) = (sqrt3/2)*sqrt(1 - r^2/4) - r/4 = 1/(2r). So at an arc width of exactly 60 degrees the pair lies exactly on the boundary of W and there is no slack, which is precisely why MC120 must keep strict < 120 degrees.

GRADE [P] RETRACTION R3: a paired block is two adjacent edge exclusions combined, E_2k union E_(2k+1), giving three labels (for example {0,1} union {1,2} = {0,1,2}); two blocks are four continua and cover at least five labels. My 2-element-block objection was a misreading of the transmitted statement, and the transmitted arithmetic needs no repair.

GRADE [P] Final EC: for blocks at vertices pairwise at cyclic distance at least 2 (the only family being {0,1,2}, {2,3,4}, {4,5,0}), every pair leaves exactly one label, so MC120 gives pairwise direction separation at least 120 degrees, and three gaps summing to 360 degrees with each at least 120 are all equal to 120: the triple is exactly equilateral. Blocks at adjacent vertices leave two labels, so only CC60's strict > 60 degrees applies and continuous families survive.

GRADE [P] A member's proposed counterexample 0/120/250 degrees does not refute EC: its circular separations are 120, 130 and 110 degrees, and 110 is below 120, so the hypothesis fails; with circular (shorter-arc) separations the three-gap argument is valid because a gap above 180 degrees forces another gap below 90. It does correctly warn that linear differences in a fixed coordinate are the wrong reading.

GRADE [S] Bank and parent facts used without re-derivation: CC60 (closed 60-degree cone cannot leave at most 2 colours) with Lean ongoing; the sharpness of the generic finite-k angle-60 statement via accepted Borel 20-colour counterexamples for wider apertures, which does not settle k = 6; R4 and the fixed/moving three-centre replacements passing local Lean with full integration pending; Lemma 6.7 = five_support_step_ban retained.

GRADE [C] m2's MC120 referee report (.ultramath/smwgpu16s/m2/MC120-referee.md, 490 lines, with check_mc120.py and check_mc120.out, mpmath 40 digits plus sympy derivatives, explicitly not Lean) independently confirmed by me on these points: S1 Straddle is a union of open sets; S2 a connected compact K meets every circle it straddles; the degeneracy clause (a single point gives Straddle empty, a nondegenerate K gives it nonempty); V1 that the literal wording of MC120 is false because a degenerate K_i empties W, and J empty forces W empty; V4 that 2r sin(sigma/2) = 1 exactly with sigma(r) < pi/3 strictly for r > 1; V5 that the a.e. step needs averaging over the rotation parameter, licensed by pulling the null bad-pair set back along (p,theta) -> (p, p + u(theta)); V6/V9 that at exactly 60 degrees the pair sits on the boundary of W, reducing the endpoint to the boundary-slope condition g >~ (sqrt3/2) eps, with threshold tau(g) = min{2 arcsin(1/(2(1+g))), arccos((1+g)/2)} tending to 60 degrees as g tends to 0.

GRADE [P] New obligation identified by m2 and accepted: the exclusion hypothesis needs an ESSENTIAL label convention (labels carried on a positive-length subset of each K_i), not merely a tangency point, because weak properness controls the circle only up to a null set; taken as a hypothesis, it is a source-level obligation (m2's O3), not a gap in MC120.

GRADE [P] m2's section 10 independently resolves the block arithmetic the same way the supervisor did: a paired block is two adjacent edge exclusions combined (three labels), so two blocks are four continua covering at least five labels; and it adds a useful correction to the transmitted wording, namely that 'three directions in a 120-degree span' is inconsistent with pairwise separation of at least 120 degrees for three distinct directions, the correct premise being pairwise separation alone, which does force the equilateral triple.

GRADE [C] m1's submission (.ultramath/smwgpu16s/m1/{MC120.md,EQUILATERAL.md,verify.py,verify_out.txt}) checked on: the missing-hypothesis counterexample; the unit-chord bound 2 arcsin(1/(2r)) < 60 degrees strictly for r > 1 with equality exactly at r = 1 (verify_out section 1); the packing theorem that three directions with pairwise circular separations at least 120 degrees are exactly equilateral (one triple on a 1-degree grid, none with four directions) and that 0/120/250 is a linear artefact with circular gaps 120, 130, 110.

GRADE [P] m1's ENGINE, accepted as the cleanest formulation: if W is open, c = a a.e. on W, and the integral over W of the one-dimensional measure of the unit circle about x intersected with W is positive, then Def 1.2 fails, because the violating pairs form a positive-measure set while a null set has a.e.-null circle sections. It consumes no rigidity lemma and no palette machinery; the 60-degree figure enters only through the sector thickness needed to make that integral positive.

GRADE [P] DECISIVE: m1's vacuity of the equilateral collapse, re-proved here without enumeration. If A, B, C are 3-element label blocks with pairwise intersections of size at most 1, then |A union B union C| = 9 - (sum of pairwise intersections) + |triple intersection| >= 9 - 3 + 0 = 6, so the union is all six labels, the residual J is empty, and W must be empty. Hence the transmitted equilateral configuration cannot occur with W nonempty: it is excluded vacuously rather than by MC120, and the correct non-vacuous statement is that at most TWO such directions can occur.

GRADE [P] m1's sector lemma is correct but conservative: the requirement w > 4 arcsin(1/(2 t0)) is twice the sharp single-chord requirement 2 arcsin(1/(2 t0)), so using the sharp factor gives aperture < 180 - 2 arcsin(1/(2 t0)) (about 151 degrees at t0 = 2) against m1's 122.09 degrees; near t0 = 1 m1's bound is weaker than the already-proved 120 degrees. The exact coincidence point t0 = (1/2) csc(15 degrees) = 1.9319 lies between the two.
conjectures: The equilateral configuration of three vertex-block continua is rigid but not excluded by CC60 plus MC120; a six-colour-specific obstruction would have to use the actual angular positions of the three blocks relative to the cycle labels, since equilateral leaves no slack in the direction parameter.

The sharp MC120 criterion is a comparison between the chord length at an admissible radius and the width of the common-positive arc, so any improvement must come from lower-bounding the strip widths delta, which in turn depends on how the K_i approach x (the size of the r_n and the deviation of w_n from v i).

If the endpoint and quantitative refinements hold up under review, the CC60 plus MC120 pair covers every configuration whose direction spread is at most 120 degrees with at most 1 residual label, and the remaining six-colour cases are exactly the three-block equilateral ones and the 2-residual families.

With the equilateral case vacuous, the six-colour common-interface stage splits as: at most two paired-block directions with pairwise union >= 5 can coexist with W nonempty; the interesting remaining configurations are therefore those leaving two or more labels, which are outside MC120 and outside CC60's reach where the directions are widely spread.
